# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 14 (Bu-Vb Pc14)
**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc14
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 14
**Title (English, from literature):** Leaving furniture outside

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 14 (*Mañcasanthārana*) is a disciplinary rule in the Vinaya Piṭaka concerning the care of communal property. The rule stipulates that a monk who spreads out or has someone spread out furniture belonging to the Saṅgha in an open space, and departs without packing it away or having it put away, incurs an offense requiring expiation (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral]. In the analysis of the rule's vocabulary, the text provides canonical definitions for various types of couches, including *masaraka*, *bundikābaddha*, *kulīrapādaka*, and *āhaccapādaka*, definitions that also serve to clarify parallel terminology in the *Khandhaka* literature [Horner]. Modern English translation of the rule is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral demonstrate that this rule has broad representation across all major surviving Vinaya lineages, including the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsaṅghika, and Dharmaguptaka traditions in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan translations, in both monks' and nuns' codes (e.g., Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 110) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus identifies extensive Pali-internal text reuse with related Vinaya rules, showing the largest shared sequences with the adjacent Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 15 (e.g., §2.1.16–2.2.3), as well as significant matches with Pācittiya 16, Pācittiya 57, the *Senāsanakkhandhaka* (Kd 16), the *Vinayasaṅgaha-aṭṭhakathā*, and the *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments by DharmaNexus also match segments of the rule to Tibetan Vinaya texts, including the *Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkāvinayasamuccaya* (D4106) and the *Bhikṣuṇīprātimokṣasūtra* (D0004) [DharmaNexus].
